Bleed the Clock

The backfield runs through one man — their top back absorbs 77% of the carries (league ~59%), a true bell-cow share that makes his rushing volume among the safest floors in the sport when the script cooperates.

The Offensive Blueprint

The WR2 is unusually involved here — 23% of targets (league ~15%), meaning there's bankable volume beyond the top receiver.

Run identity is the through-line here: PHI call pass on -6% of snaps relative to what the situation expects (league -2%), and when they get ahead they lean even harder on the ground — just 37% pass on early downs with a lead. This is a ball-control operation built to shorten games.

They lean on tempo — a 23% no-huddle rate (league ~11%) that inflates snap counts and everyone's volume.

They live in the shotgun (81% of snaps vs ~68%) — a spread, pass-oriented structure.

In the Red Zone

Inside the 20 they lean run-heavy, passing 36% of the time, funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back.

Defense — A Balanced Defense

They lock down opposing tight ends — just 25 rec yds/game (vs ~35); fade receiving props there.

Soft against opposing WR2s — 42 rec yds/game (vs ~36). A rec-yards target.

They lock down opposing WR1s — just 52 rec yds/game (vs ~58); fade receiving props there.

They surrender 112 rushing and 208 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). No dominant funnel — read it matchup by matchup.

A stingy, efficient defense — just 41% success allowed (vs ~44%); temper expectations for opposing skill players.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: back their RB1's rushing volume in favored/positive scripts.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
